newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Two firms could form Portugal's biggest builder.
newsitem.headline: Two firms could form Portugal's biggest builder.

text.p: Civil engineering group Somague and building firm A.Silva & Silva are holding talks that could lead to the creation of Portugal's biggest construction group, analysts said on Thursday.
The two firms announced on Wednesday that they had held talks about a possible exchange of shares.
One option would be for Somague, which has specialised in public works projects, to acquire some or all of the construction interests of A.Silva & Silva, a statement said.
Analysts said Somague wanted to buy A.Silva & Silva's building subsidiary Assiconstroi, which is active in private and public sector residential, commercial and industrial building.
They said the deal for at least 10 billion escudos ($60 million), which could be concluded in weeks, would make Somague Portugal's biggest construction group, surpassing Soares da Costa.
"Somague wants to diversify away from a heavy reliance on public works projects towards greater involvement in private sector projects," said Mark Howard of Lloyds Bank Fund Managers.
He estimated that Somague could acquire a market share of up to 10 percent of total construction works in Portugal if the acquisition went ahead, up from around five percent now.

Analysts said that Somague, which is heavily dependent on road, water and dam projects, was seeking to diversify away from infrastructure building as European Union development funds for Portugal would dry up by the end of the century.

They said the firm saw the acquisition of Assiconstroi as an ideal way to boost its involvement in the private sector where overall construction demand was growing steadily at around five percent a year. Portugal faces an acute housing shortage.
The acquisition would strengthen Somague's cash flow and growth prospects into the 21st century, a source familiar with Portuguese construction said.

"Somague has the prospect of another two years of top-line growth in public works projects. The time has come when it has to choose between being a niche specialist or becoming the biggest player in the sector," the source said.
Analysts said that Somague could also acquire A.Silva & Silva's road building subsidiary Sopol, its maintenance company MGT and its foundations firm Geosoc, depending on the progress of the talks.
Somague and A.Silva & Silva have not supplied any details of their conversations.
Somague's share price fell by almost 10 percent to 1,900 escudos in morning trade on Lisbon bourse, while A.Silva & Silva shares hit a high of 1,900 escudos.
